title: Federal prosecutors announce dismantling of 'marriage fraud ring' in Massachusetts

 Federal prosecutors in Massachusetts on Wednesday announced that they've dismantled an alleged marriage fraud ring that arranged hundreds of sham marriages.
 U.S. Attorney Leah Foley said the sham marriages were designed to obtain unlawful immigration benefits.
 Six people -- five from Fall River and one from Attleboro -- were charged.
 The alleged mastermind behind the scheme is a U.S. citizen, born in the United States. Foley said her name is Jennifer Gonzalez.
 She said Gonzalez is responsible for fraudulently arranging sham marriages in Massachusetts for over a decade.
 The US Attorney for Massachusetts released this image of what it said is a contract with one of Gonzalez's customers. 
 She allegedly charged between $38,000 and $40,000 per marriage and arranged 18 to 20 marriages a year, for over 10 years.
 Foley said the marriage fraud ring generated over $6 million in profit.
 "They would get married, they would stay married for a couple of years, three years, they would get divorced, a month later they would remarry another illegal alien," Foley said. "It was long enough so that it wasn't suspicious, it wasn't three weeks later."

 Foley said her office was made aware of the scheme after someone came forward.
 She said a cooperating witness recorded Gonzalez when she admitted to what she does with the money generated. Foley says in her words, she bragged about investing the money in business and property in the Dominican Republic.
 The U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts released this image of what it said was a sham marriage involving one of the defendants. 
 Gonzalez also allegedly applied for and received SNAP benefits between 2019 and 2026.
 She did not list her income from her sham marriage business or anybody else in her household.
 The defendants were identified as:
 Jennifer Gonzalez, 43, of Fall River
 Erica Daniels, 29, of Fall River
 Chreise Alejandro, 39), of Fall River
 Amara Pugh, 31, of Fall River
 Jessica Tavares, 31, of Attleboro
 Jaylin Hill, 26, of Fall River
 Officials from Homeland Security Investigations and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services also spoke at a news conference in Boston announcing the charges.
